From coursework to a reproducible study

The original notebook explores regression, feature selection and multiclass classification. The portfolio edition uses an R kernel, removes source/row indicators, learns missing-value handling on training rows and evaluates on one held-out split.

New 200-tree Random Forest baselines with training-only feature preparation. These scores are separate from the original coursework experiments.

NEW PORTFOLIO RUN / 31 OCTOBER 2026

Explore the evidence.

400 training rows / 100 validation rows per task · fixed 80/20 split · seed 42

Loading notebook results…

Results were produced by executing the same source code included in the downloadable portfolio notebook. Original advanced-model scores are not presented as reproduced results. Input datasets are retained locally and are excluded from the code download.

What the results tell me

Happiness regression RMSE is 7.8807 versus 12.7851 for the training-mean baseline on the same validation rows. Classification accuracy is 0.36 versus 0.28 for the majority baseline; macro-F1 is 0.3133. Classification remains a weak result requiring further investigation.

Limitations & next improvements

Limits of this study

  • A single split of a small survey dataset gives uncertain estimates.
  • Self-reported labels and associations do not establish causes or diagnoses.
  • The baseline is not the full original XGBoost/SMOTE experiment.
  • No clinical use or fairness across demographic groups is established.

What I would do next

  1. Use repeated stratified evaluation and report uncertainty.
  2. Inspect per-class errors and survey-label quality.
  3. Document feature meaning and subgroup performance before extending the work.
